articles.headline: Pep Guardiola set to attend first Man City home game since guilty verdict - sources
articles.description: Pep Guardiola is expected to attend Manchester City's Champions League fixture against Paris Saint-Germain, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: ペップ・グアルディオラ、有罪判決後初となるマンチェスター・シティのホームゲームに出席へ（関係者談）
articles.descriptionJa: 関係者がESPNに語ったところによると、ペップ・グアルディオラはマンチェスター・シティのチャンピオンズリーグ、パリ・サンジェルマン戦に出席する見込みだ。
articles.body:
Pep Guardiola is expected to attend Manchester City's Champions League fixture against Paris Saint-Germain, sources have told ESPN, the club's first home game since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Guardiola is set to be in the stands at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday for the first time since quitting as manager at the end of last season.

The timing of the 55-year-old's return is significant, coming in the wake of the damning verdict in City's case with the Premier League.

In the aftermath of the publication of the independent commission's findings, Guardiola released a statement in support of his former club.

He posted on social media: "I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here more than ever.

"I am, always have been, always will be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

City have maintained their innocence throughout the process and have filed a formal appeal. Both chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano have insisted publicly that the club will be cleared.

- Ian Darke's early Premier League impressions for all 20 teams

- Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo in doubt for Liverpool vs. Man City clash

- We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero

The financial breaches which form the basis of the Premier League's case occured between 2009 and 2018. Guardiola became City boss in 2016 and won 20 trophies during a 10-year spell.

City face Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday before returning to the Etihad to play reigning European champions PSG three days later.

articles.headline: NBA, FIBA say Europe push to continue without EuroLeague
articles.description: The NBA and FIBA say they are undeterred in moving forward with the NBA Europe plan after EuroLeague's team owners rejected a merger offer this week.
articles.headlineJa: NBAとFIBA、ユーロリーグ抜きでの欧州展開継続を表明
articles.descriptionJa: ユーロリーグのチームオーナーたちが今週、合併案を拒否したことを受け、NBAとFIBAは「NBA Europe」計画を推進する意志に変わりはないと述べている。
articles.body:
MACAO -- In the wake of EuroLeague team owners rejecting a merger offer this week, the NBA has answered back: NBA Europe is moving forward anyway.

On Thursday, the NBA and FIBA, the sport's international governing body and partner with the league on the developing venture, released a joint statement making it clear they are undeterred.

"A partnership between the EuroLeague, FIBA and the NBA to unify the European basketball ecosystem would unlock the game's enormous potential across Europe for the benefit of clubs, players and, most importantly, fans," they said. "The NBA and FIBA remain committed to moving forward with a new professional men's league in Europe and helping build a stronger, more sustainable basketball ecosystem alongside partners who share our vision of growth, opportunity and the core principles of the European sports model."

Though this back-and-forth is revealing a rising tension between the two leagues after months of discussions, there is still an open door to negotiate, sources told ESPN.

Last month, after nearly two years of development, the NBA presented a formal merger offer to the EuroLeague. The EuroLeague leadership met this week on the banks of Lake Como in Italy and voted to turn down the NBA's offer, believing it undervalued the value of the league, sources said.

They also reportedly discussed expanding the European league beyond its current 13 license holders, a saber-rattling move designed to potentially block the NBA from certain cities and partners. However, multiple members of the EuroLeague have had extensive talks with the NBA and are believed to be seriously interested in joining a new NBA Europe.

EuroLeague member Barcelona said this week that team and the league would be open to considering an amended offer from the NBA and FIBA.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver and deputy commissioner Mark Tatum, who has been running point on the European project, are in Macao this week for the league's China Games featuring the Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks. They are in the midst of meetings and events with Asian partners, but their focus has been on this developing situation in Europe.

The NBA has collected expansion offers on new franchises throughout Western Europe, has interest from existing teams and plans a 16-team league to start as early as 2027.

The EuroLeague was formed in 2001 after two rival leagues, one of them operated by FIBA, battled each other for a season. The league expanded to 20 teams in 2025-26, with seven clubs qualifying through their domestic leagues or via invitation.

articles.headline: The Warriors need Yaxel Lendeborg's fast-tracked development
articles.description: The Golden State Warriors have high hopes for the No. 11 pick after several failed lottery picks.
articles.headlineJa: ウォリアーズ、ヤクセル・レンデボーグの早期育成を必要としている
articles.descriptionJa: ゴールデンステート・ウォリアーズは、これまでのドラフト・ロトでの失敗が続いたこともあり、指名11位の選手に大きな期待を寄せている。
articles.body:
THE WEEK PRIOR to training camp, every Golden State Warriors player gathered at Jimmy Butler's mansion in San Diego and competed in a handful of pickup games.

In his lone game paired with Stephen Curry and Draymond Green, rookie wing Yaxel Lendeborg found himself near the elbow during a frontcourt inbound. As the ball was delivered to Green up top, Curry cut toward Lendeborg to set a back screen. Both defenders remained with Curry and Lendeborg, sensing it, slipped backdoor and received a pass from Green for an uncontested dunk.

"'That's all year! All year!'" Green and Curry roared at Lendeborg with ferocity, according to the rookie. "Super loud and aggressive."

In Lendeborg's mind, he made the simple read within the flow, using Curry's gravity for two easy points. It represented something far bigger for Green and Curry. Their newest weapon was already recognizing and leveraging the patterns that make the Warriors' offense hum, signaling a readiness to help the team win before the two franchise legends age out of the league.

"It looked like we had been playing together for a long time," Green said.

On their final draft board in June, the Warriors -- who owned the No. 11 pick -- had Lendeborg and Arizona guard Brayden Burries ranked neck-and-neck, behind the consensus group of prospects up top. If Burries was there, team sources have indicated they would've drafted the 20-year-old combo guard for his upside. He had fans all over the organization.

But the Milwaukee Bucks, selecting 10th, took away that option. The Warriors quickly pivoted to Lendeborg, adding the older prospect they believed fit their immediate timeline and urgency of Curry's final seasons.

"He's massive," Butler said. "Just a big human being."

At 24 years old and 241 pounds, standing 6-foot-9 with a 7-foot-4 wingspan, Lendeborg has the size and power of a mid-prime wing on a Warriors roster that is currently thin and injured at that spot, waiting for Butler and Moses Moody to return from lengthy rehabs for serious knee injuries.

Lendeborg won over Steve Kerr in the predraft process, impressing the Warriors coach during a film session because of his knowledge of the game paired with charisma and his willingness to learn.

"Unbelievably coachable," Kerr said after Tuesday night's preseason win over the Los Angeles Lakers.

The organization has been impressed that, after a long national title run at Michigan that included an MCL and ankle sprain in the NCAA tournament, Lendeborg took his offseason work seriously, played in eight summer league games and led them to a Las Vegas title.

Then he showed up at training camp and Kerr inserted him into the starting lineup, showing a belief that he can be a small forward in a lineup that includes Green and a center or a power forward next to Green in smaller groupings.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタ「アーセナルのCL決勝敗戦の傷跡は今も残っている」
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタは、5月に行われたパリ・サンジェルマンとのチャンピオンズリーグ決勝での敗戦による「傷跡」がいまだに残っていると語った。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

articles.headline: What does your NBA team need? The biggest hole on all 30 rosters
articles.description: Every NBA team is missing something, even the leading title contenders.
articles.headlineJa: あなたのNBAチームに足りないものは？ 全30チームのロスターにおける最大の弱点
articles.descriptionJa: 優勝候補の有力チームであっても、すべてのNBAチームには何かしらの欠けている要素がある。
articles.body:
In the NBA's second apron era, deep rosters don't stay deep forever, team identities can flip at a moment's notice, and money can prompt painful divorces.

This summer alone, the 2026 champion New York Knicks lost beloved backup center Mitchell Robinson, the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder shed three rotation players in cost-cutting trades, and the 2024 champion Boston Celtics traded away Finals MVP Jaylen Brown. Meanwhile, the Minnesota Timberwolves sacrificed frontcourt depth to assemble a tantalizing backcourt duo, and LeBron James said goodbye to the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons.

Let's take stock of all 30 teams now that the offseason dust has settled and the preseason is in full swing. With so many salary cap rules preventing teams from aggregating talent, everybody is missing something, even the leading title contenders. But what, exactly, is each team's biggest hole?

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks

Roster hole: Superstar centerpiece

The Hawks have methodically constructed a balanced rotation with healthy doses of ballhandling, outside shooting and on-ball defense. After adding championship experience by nabbing Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins from the Oklahoma City Thunder in offseason trades, Atlanta's biggest question is whether Jalen Johnson can elevate from All-Star to superstar.

The do-everything forward saw his impressive regular-season numbers dip dramatically in a first-round series loss to the Knicks, but he's still only 24 years old. Can he develop into an offensive fulcrum capable of leading a deep playoff run?

The Hawks can be patient in their assessment as they boast enough salary cap flexibility and draft assets to explore a big-name addition down the road.

Johnson is entering the second year of a team-friendly extension worth $150 million over five seasons, and none of Atlanta's other core pieces are on the books for more than $25 million this season.

Boston Celtics

Roster hole: Free throw generator

While the Celtics' decision to trade Brown for Paul George made sense as a long-term financial play, it created two immediate problems on the court. First, the 36-year-old George played less than half as many minutes as the 29-year-old Brown last season. Second, George attempted only 111 free throws in 2025-26 -- a far cry from Brown's 536, which easily represented a career high.

George's perimeter shooting and experience playing off high-usage stars should make him a good fit next to Jayson Tatum in coach Joe Mazzulla's 3-point heavy system, but Boston will need to find a way to replace Brown's ability to work inside the arc and draw contact. The Celtics ranked last in free throw attempts last season even though Brown ranked fifth in the NBA.

articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール・価値変動ウォッチ：上昇中のボストン、下落中のハーツ
articles.descriptionJa: マット・ボーエンが、開幕から1ヶ月が経過して評価が上がっている選手と、逆に勢いを失っている選手をリストアップする。
articles.body:
Four games into the 2026 NFL season, fantasy football managers are starting to get a better feel for their rosters. We see scheme trends developing that impact player upside and usage (both positively and negatively), which can lead to smarter decisions when setting our weekly lineups.

It's also a reminder that the summer hype -- and talk of breakout players -- doesn't always hit once the games are played. Those players we had up high on our draft boards? Some of them are barely hanging on in the lineup, while there are also players emerging at an accelerated rate who need to be in starting slots.

Below are four ascending players and four more who are trending in the opposite direction heading into the Week 5 slate of games.

Stock rising

Denzel Boston, WR, Cleveland Browns

I'd have Boston locked into my lineup as a high-ceiling WR3/flex given his route deployment and explosive-play potential. Boston has scored 12 or more points in three of four games, with a touchdown reception in two. Plus, he's seeing 5.5 targets per game with a route tree that is expanding.

The deep shots from quarterback Deshaun Watson show up on the tape, as Boston has seen eight targets on throws of 15 or more air yards, but the rookie can also uncover on slants, out routes and comebacks. Looking at his play speed and ball-tracking ability, I see big upside for Boston, with the Jets, Ravens and Titans up next.

Deebo Samuel Sr., WR, San Francisco 49ers

Samuel has scored at least 15 points in three of four games, and he is being used exactly how we thought he would be in Kyle Shanahan's offense.

In a tough Week 4 matchup versus the Denver defense, Samuel caught five passes for 26 yards and a touchdown and added 44 yards rushing on three carries, good for 18 fantasy points. Backfield alignments (and carries), screens, crossers and unders. Shanahan will use Samuel, who is a power strider, on concepts that give him a long runway and space to display his vision and physical play style.

Now, the Week 5 matchup versus the Seattle defense isn't ideal, but Samuel gets the Commanders and Falcons, who both rank in the bottom five against opposing wide receivers, in Weeks 6 and 7, respectively. Samuel is a WR3 in 12-team leagues, and the arrow is pointing up for the veteran in this offense.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Chicago Bears

The Bears' ability to dominate game flow and time of possession in the Week 4 win over the Jets boosted the totals for Monangai, who scored a career-high 28 fantasy points, rushing for 146 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries. He was really decisive with the ball.

Monangai saw seven goal-to-go carries in the game (converting two for touchdowns), while D'Andre Swift struggled in the low red zone. In addition, a second-half Swift fumble prompted coach Ben Johnson to roll with Monangai to close out the game.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: André Snellings' Ultimate Draft Board
articles.description: André Snellings crunches the numbers, factors in average draft position and highlights the best spots to draft key players throughout your fantasy basketball draft.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・バスケットボール：アンドレ・スネリングの究極のドラフトボード
articles.descriptionJa: アンドレ・スネリングが数値を分析し、平均ドラフト順位（ADP）を考慮した上で、ファンタジー・バスケットボール・ドラフトにおいて主要な選手を指名すべき最適なタイミングを提示する。
articles.body:
What does your perfect fantasy basketball draft look like?

This is a question you should consider before your draft begins, when you're still in the planning stages. Even now, after all these years of playing fantasy sports, I still do this before most big drafts.

I look at where I'm picking in the draft and decide who, among those likely to be there, I'll take first. Then I'll look at where my next picks will be and compare that to the player rankings, to see who I would most want among players in the right range for me to potentially take them. 

Having that plan in place can help you enter your fantasy basketball draft with a clearer idea of what you want to accomplish. Most of the people in your leagues aren't going to go into the draft with much of a plan and will instead just hope for the best. So, if you step into the draft with an idea about what the talent looks like at different parts of the draft, it will give you a leg up on the competition right from the opening tip.

The best way to gauge what your team might look like, in my experience, is to do mock draft(s) before my real drafts to get a feel for what players should be available. Will my sleeper picks be there, or does everyone know about them so they go earlier than expected?

Often, there are really good players ranked lower than you might expect that might be available later than you think they should be. Having an idea of how this tends to shake out before you enter your draft can be very valuable for maximizing your squad.

In this article, I highlight players I would like to draft at different locations within the draft. In the early rounds, draft slot makes a huge difference in what players might be available, so I point out players of interest in different parts of the round.

In the middle and later rounds, I highlight groups of players that I like that should be available in that range.

To determine likelihood of availability, I utilize Average Draft Pick (ADP) data to offer insight on the type of value that might be available throughout your own drafts.

Note: ADPs are current as of date of publish. Click here for the latest.

The foundation

Round 1: Still playing the Joker card

If I have the first pick in a points league, I'm taking Nikola Jokic (ADP 1.5) immediately. He has been the top fantasy scorer for six straight seasons, and has averaged a triple-double in two straight. He not only projects as the top player this season, but is projected to outscore second place by more than 500 fantasy points. That's larger than the gap between the bottom of the first round and a mid-late fourth round pick.

In category leagues, there is a legitimate debate whether to take Jokic or Victor Wembanyama (ADP 3.1) first. Wembanyama's league-leading shot-blocking is very valuable in category leagues, and with his strong across-the-board contributions and ever-improving game (he is still only 22 years old!) he is a justifiable top pick even over the dominant Jokic.

articles.headline: Raúl Asencio on drink driving conviction: 'I'm at Real Madrid, that can't happen again'
articles.description: Raúl Asencio has said he is only focused on winning at Real Madrid and "turning the situation around" following his recent conviction for drink driving.
articles.headlineJa: ラウル・アセンシオ、飲酒運転での有罪判決について語る：「レアル・マドリードにいる身として、二度と同じことは起こさない」
articles.descriptionJa: ラウル・アセンシオは、最近の飲酒運転による有罪判決を受け、レアル・マドリードでの勝利にのみ集中し、「状況を好転させる」と語った。
articles.body:
Raúl Asencio has said he is only focused on winning at Real Madrid and "turning the situation around" following his recent conviction for drink driving.

The Spanish centre-back was fined €14,400 (£12,208 / $16,103) on Sept. 2 and had his driver's licence suspended for eight months having admitted to driving under the influence of alcohol after testing positive at a sobriety checkpoint.

"It was a really tough time," Asencio told Diario AS. "Several things in my life coincided within a short space of time."

One day after his DUI conviction, Asencio was acquitted by a Spanish court of charges related to allegedly recording sexual images of a woman and a minor and distributing them without their consent.

Real Madrid opened a disciplinary proceeding against Asencio after his drink driving conviction, with coach José Mourinho stressing that a "Madrid player is 24 hours a day, seven days a week and 12 months a year."

Asencio, who was promoted to Madrid's first team in the summer of 2024, agreed.

"He [Mourinho] was absolutely right," he said. "Ultimately, people form opinions based on what's reported and what they see. I made a mistake. I admitted it then and I admit it now; I've apologised and I'll continue to do so. I'm a 23-year-old lad and I've made mistakes, just as we all do at that age.

"But I have to be aware of where I am. I'm at Real Madrid and that can't happen again. I'm taking this seriously and my only focus is on turning this situation around. I'm the one who's most upset about it.

- Mourinho already has a lot to do to save Real Madrid's season

- Getafe president: Deal for ex-Real Madrid defender Dani Carvajal is off

"I dream of turning it all around and winning trophies with this club and in this shirt -- hopefully for the rest of my career. That's why situations like this won't happen again."

Asencio made 34 appearances for Madrid in the 2025-26 campaign.

Injuries have prevented Asencio from playing for Madrid this season, with the player currently sidelined until next year after having surgery for a stress fracture in his right tibia on Oct. 1.

articles.headline: How to bet Bucs-Cowboys on TNF: Analysis, tips and top prop plays
articles.description: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.headlineJa: TNFでのバックス対カウボーイズ戦の賭け方：分析、ヒント、おすすめのプロップベット
articles.descriptionJa: 「サーズデー・ナイト・フットボール」で行われるタンパベイ・バッカニアーズ対ダラス・カウボーイズ戦のベッティングに役立つオッズ、賭け方、分析を紹介。
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys head into Week 5 at 2-2, coming off a 34-30 win in Houston. Dak Prescott is playing at an extremely high level for an explosive Cowboys offense, completing 70% of his throws (fourth highest in the league), while running this system like a point guard. CeeDee Lamb, who had a career-high 17 receptions (on 21 targets) in the win over Houston, paces the wide receivers room, while George Pickens offers big-play ability on the perimeter. Javonte Williams is the downhill hammer in the run game for a unit that is scoring 30.5 PPG. The defense, under new coordinator Christian Parker, has yet to form its 2026 identity, allowing 28.0 points and 389.5 yards per game, which both rank in the bottom five of the league. But this group has the talent -- and the scheme -- to match up with a Tampa Bay Buccaneers offense that will be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb).

The 0-4 Buccaneers started undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels in the Week 4 loss to the Packers. We saw a lot of quick-game concepts, screens and defined reads for Daniels, but he did make some throws while bringing an added element as a dual-threat player on designed carries and scrambles (eight rushes, 55 yards). The Buccaneers will look to control tempo with Bucky Irving and the ground game against a Dallas defense surrendering 150.3 rushing yards per game (second most in the league), while the passing game will need to generate more vertical throws for Daniels. On defense, we know Todd Bowles' unit will try to heat up Prescott (38.2% blitz rate) with more zone coverage in the secondary to limit explosive plays over the top.

Betting outlook

I'm going to follow the trends and what we've seen from both clubs over the first four weeks of the season. As I mentioned before, the Bucs set up Daniels last week with throws that allowed him to make quick reads and play as a ball distributor in his first pro start. That should continue against a Dallas defense that has struggled to limit opposing quarterbacks (239.9 passing yards per game). And Irving should play a volume role on the ground.

The same can be said for Lamb and his consistent usage in the pass game (at least eight targets in each game). Look for throws that target coverage voids, which increase his numbers Thursday night. I like the Tampa Bay defense to hold Javonte Williams' yardage totals in check, though he might find the end zone. The Buccaneers are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per game.
